exposure: mode of delivery after failed vacuum (second instrument vs. cesarean section)
Mode of delivery after failed vacuum (second instrument vs. cesarean)
cohort: 172 mothers who had a failed vacuum delivery between January 2006 and December 2014
finding: The use of a second instrument after failed vacuum delivery was associated with a higher prevalence of third-degree perineal tears and episiotomy but did not significantly increase neonatal morbidity compared to cesarean section.
mod_finding: While second instrument delivery after failed vacuum did not increase overall neonatal morbidity compared to cesarean, if the second instrument also failed, neonatal morbidity was significantly increased (longer stay in neonatal unit, lower pH, lower Apgar scores, more intubation and seizures).
